problem: pip install fails with 'Permission denied' error when installing packages globally
error_code: PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied
symptoms: Running pip install package_name fails with a permission error. The error occurs when pip tries to write to the site-packages directory.
attempted_steps: Tried running pip install directly in command prompt
supporting_evidence: Python packages should be installed in virtual environments to avoid permission issues with the global site-packages directory.
verified_solution:
1. Create a virtual environment: python -m venv myenv
2. Activate it: myenv\Scripts\activate (Windows) or source myenv/bin/activate (Linux/macOS)
3. Then install: pip install package_name

Alternatively, use --user flag: pip install --user package_name

problem: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'numpy' even though pip install numpy succeeded
error_code: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'numpy'
symptoms: pip install numpy shows 'Requirement already satisfied' but running python -c 'import numpy' fails with ModuleNotFoundError
attempted_steps: Ran pip install numpy, tried pip install --force-reinstall numpy
supporting_evidence: This typically occurs when pip and python point to different Python installations. Running 'pip' might install to Python 3.10 while 'python' runs Python 3.11.
verified_solution:
1. Verify which Python pip is using: pip --version (check the path)
2. Verify which Python you're running: python --version and 'where python'
3. Use the matching pair: python -m pip install numpy
4. Or create a venv to avoid confusion: python -m venv venv && venv\Scripts\activate && pip install numpy

problem: pip install fails with 'ERROR: Could not build wheels' for packages with C extensions
error_code: ERROR: Could not build wheels for package_name
symptoms: Installing packages like numpy, pandas, or lxml fails during the build step. Error messages mention missing Microsoft Visual C++ Build Tools.
attempted_steps: Tried pip install package_name, tried pip install --no-cache-dir package_name
supporting_evidence: Some Python packages contain C extensions that need to be compiled. On Windows, this requires Microsoft Visual C++ Build Tools.
verified_solution:
Option 1: Install pre-built wheels
pip install --only-binary :all: package_name

Option 2: Install Build Tools
1. Download Visual Studio Build Tools from https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/visual-cpp-build-tools/
2. Install 'Desktop development with C++' workload
3. Restart terminal and retry pip install

Option 3: Use conda instead
conda install package_name

problem: Virtual environment activation fails: 'running scripts is disabled on this system' on Windows PowerShell
error_code: cannot be loaded because running scripts is disabled on this system
symptoms: After creating a venv with python -m venv myenv, running myenv\Scripts\activate in PowerShell fails with a script execution policy error.
attempted_steps: Created venv with python -m venv myenv, tried activating with .\myenv\Scripts\activate
supporting_evidence: Windows PowerShell has an execution policy that blocks script execution by default for security.
verified_solution:
Option 1: Change execution policy for current user
Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser
Then activate: .\myenv\Scripts\activate

Option 2: Use CMD instead of PowerShell
cmd
myenv\Scripts\activate.bat

Option 3: Use the activate.bat directly in PowerShell
cmd /k myenv\Scripts\activate.bat

problem: pip install shows 'WARNING: pip is configured with locations that require TLS/SSL, however the ssl module in Python is not available'
error_code: WARNING: pip is configured with locations that require TLS/SSL, however the ssl module in Python is not available
symptoms: pip install fails with SSL-related warnings. Cannot download any packages from PyPI. Python was compiled from source without SSL support.
attempted_steps: Tried pip install, tried pip install --trusted-host pypi.org
supporting_evidence: When Python is compiled from source, it needs OpenSSL development headers to build the ssl module.
verified_solution:
1. Install OpenSSL development headers:
   Ubuntu/Debian: sudo apt install libssl-dev libffi-dev
   CentOS/RHEL: sudo yum install openssl-devel
2. Rebuild Python from source:
   cd Python-3.10.x
   ./configure --with-openssl=/usr
   make
   sudo make install

Alternative: Use pyenv which handles this automatically:
   sudo apt install libssl-dev libffi-dev
   pyenv install 3.10

problem: git push rejected: 'Updates were rejected because the remote contains work that you do not have locally'
error_code: error: failed to push some refs; Updates were rejected because the remote contains work that you do not have locally
symptoms: Running git push origin main fails. Someone else has pushed commits to the remote that are not in the local repository.
attempted_steps: Tried git push, tried git push --force
supporting_evidence: Git rejects pushes when the remote has commits that aren't in the local history to prevent data loss.
verified_solution:
1. First, pull the remote changes:
   git pull origin main --rebase
2. Resolve any merge conflicts if they appear
3. Then push again:
   git push origin main

WARNING: Do NOT use --force unless you understand you will overwrite remote history. If you must force push (e.g., after rebase):
   git push --force-with-lease origin main
   (--force-with-lease is safer than --force as it checks for unexpected remote changes)

problem: git merge conflict: 'CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in filename'
error_code: CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict
symptoms: After running git merge or git pull, files show conflict markers (<<<<<<< HEAD, =======, >>>>>>> branch). Git reports automatic merge failed.
attempted_steps: Ran git merge feature-branch, saw conflict markers in files
supporting_evidence: Merge conflicts occur when Git cannot automatically reconcile changes in the same part of a file from different branches.
verified_solution:
1. See which files have conflicts:
   git status
2. Open each conflicted file and look for conflict markers:
   <<<<<<< HEAD
   (your changes)
   =======
   (their changes)
   >>>>>>> branch-name
3. Edit the file to keep the desired code (remove markers)
4. Stage resolved files:
   git add resolved_file.py
5. Complete the merge:
   git commit

Tip: Use a visual merge tool:
   git mergetool

problem: Git asks for username and password on every push despite setting up SSH keys
error_code: Username for 'https://github.com':
symptoms: Every git push or pull asks for GitHub username and password. SSH keys are generated but git still uses HTTPS.
attempted_steps: Generated SSH keys with ssh-keygen, added public key to GitHub
supporting_evidence: Git remote URL determines the authentication method. HTTPS remotes use username/password while SSH remotes use SSH keys.
verified_solution:
The remote URL is set to HTTPS instead of SSH.

1. Check current remote URL:
   git remote -v
2. If it shows https://github.com/..., change to SSH:
   git remote set-url origin git@github.com:username/repo.git
3. Test SSH connection:
   ssh -T git@github.com
4. Now git push should use SSH keys without password prompts

Alternative: Keep HTTPS and use credential caching:
   git config --global credential.helper cache
   git config --global credential.helper 'cache --timeout=3600'

problem: Python ImportError: attempted relative import with no known parent package
error_code: ImportError: attempted relative import with no known parent package
symptoms: Running a Python script directly with 'python script.py' fails when the script uses relative imports like 'from .module import function'
attempted_steps: Tried running the script directly: python mypackage/script.py
supporting_evidence: Relative imports require the module to be part of a package. Running a script directly doesn't set up the package context.
verified_solution:
1. Run the module as part of a package using -m flag:
   python -m mypackage.script
   (from the parent directory of mypackage)

2. Make sure __init__.py exists in the package directory

3. Alternative: Add the parent directory to sys.path at the top of the script:
   import sys
   from pathlib import Path
   sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent.parent))

4. Best practice: Set up a proper package with setup.py or pyproject.toml and install in editable mode:
   pip install -e .

problem: pip install hangs or is extremely slow when downloading packages
error_code: ReadTimeoutError: HTTPSConnectionPool
symptoms: pip install takes forever or times out. Downloads start but proceed very slowly or hang at 'Downloading...'
attempted_steps: Tried pip install multiple times, tried at different times of day
supporting_evidence: Slow pip installs can be caused by network issues, DNS resolution problems, or the default PyPI mirror being far from the user's location.
verified_solution:
1. Increase timeout:
   pip install --timeout 100 package_name

2. Use a faster mirror:
   pip install -i https://pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/simple package_name
   Or set permanently:
   pip config set global.index-url https://pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/simple

3. Use --no-cache-dir if cache is corrupted:
   pip install --no-cache-dir package_name

4. Check proxy settings:
   pip install --proxy http://proxy:port package_name

5. Try pip install with verbose mode to see where it stalls:
   pip install -v package_name

problem: Git detached HEAD state: 'You are in detached HEAD state'
error_code: You are in 'detached HEAD' state
symptoms: Git shows 'HEAD detached at commit-hash'. Commits made in this state seem to disappear when switching branches.
attempted_steps: Checked out a specific commit with git checkout abc1234
supporting_evidence: Detached HEAD occurs when you checkout a specific commit, tag, or remote branch directly instead of a local branch.
verified_solution:
To get back to a branch:
1. If you haven't made any commits in detached state:
   git checkout main  (or your branch name)

2. If you made commits you want to keep:
   git branch save-my-work  (create a branch at current position)
   git checkout main
   git merge save-my-work

3. To prevent detached HEAD when checking out a remote branch:
   Instead of: git checkout origin/feature
   Use: git checkout feature  (creates local tracking branch)
   Or: git switch feature

problem: Python version conflict: 'python' command runs Python 2.7 instead of Python 3
error_code: SyntaxError: invalid syntax (for Python 3 syntax in Python 2)
symptoms: Running 'python' launches Python 2.7 even though Python 3 is installed. Scripts with Python 3 syntax fail with SyntaxError.
attempted_steps: Installed Python 3 via apt, tried running scripts with 'python script.py'
supporting_evidence: Many Linux distributions have both Python 2 and Python 3 installed, with 'python' aliased to Python 2 for legacy compatibility.
verified_solution:
1. Use python3 explicitly:
   python3 script.py
   python3 -m pip install package

2. Check installed versions:
   python --version
   python3 --version
   which python
   which python3

3. Create an alias (add to ~/.bashrc):
   alias python=python3
   alias pip=pip3

4. Use update-alternatives (Debian/Ubuntu):
   sudo update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/python python /usr/bin/python3 1

5. Best practice: Always use venv which pins the Python version:
   python3 -m venv myenv
   source myenv/bin/activate

problem: pip install requirements.txt fails: 'ERROR: No matching distribution found'
error_code: ERROR: No matching distribution found for package==version
symptoms: Running pip install -r requirements.txt fails because one or more packages have version constraints that don't match available versions for the current Python version or platform.
attempted_steps: Tried pip install -r requirements.txt
supporting_evidence: Package version constraints in requirements.txt may not be compatible with the current Python version or operating system.
verified_solution:
1. Check which package is failing and look up available versions:
   pip install package_name==  (shows all available versions)

2. Check Python version compatibility:
   python --version
   (Some packages drop support for older Python versions)

3. Update the version constraint in requirements.txt:
   Change: package==1.0.0
   To: package>=1.0.0 or package~=1.0

4. Try installing without version pins:
   pip install package_name
   Then freeze: pip freeze > requirements.txt

5. If using an older requirements.txt, update all at once:
   pip install --upgrade -r requirements.txt

problem: Git refuses to merge unrelated histories
error_code: fatal: refusing to merge unrelated histories
symptoms: When trying to pull from or merge with a remote repository, Git refuses because the local and remote repositories have completely different commit histories.
attempted_steps: Created a new repo on GitHub with README, then tried to push existing local repo to it
supporting_evidence: This happens when you initialize a new GitHub repo with a README/license and then try to connect an existing local repo to it.
verified_solution:
1. Allow merging unrelated histories:
   git pull origin main --allow-unrelated-histories

2. Resolve any conflicts that arise, then commit

3. Better approach for new repos: Create the GitHub repo WITHOUT initializing it (no README, .gitignore, or license), then:
   git remote add origin https://github.com/user/repo.git
   git push -u origin main

4. If you want to start fresh from remote:
   git fetch origin
   git reset --hard origin/main
   WARNING: This will discard all local commits

problem: Python virtual environment uses wrong Python version
error_code: python: No module named venv
symptoms: Creating a virtual environment with 'python -m venv myenv' creates it with Python 3.8 instead of the desired Python 3.12. Or 'python -m venv' fails because venv is not installed.
attempted_steps: Ran python -m venv myenv, checked python version inside venv
supporting_evidence: The venv module creates virtual environments using the Python interpreter that invoked it.
verified_solution:
1. Install venv for your Python version (if missing):
   sudo apt install python3.12-venv

2. Create venv with the specific Python version:
   python3.12 -m venv myenv
   (Use the full version-specific command)

3. Verify the correct version:
   source myenv/bin/activate
   python --version

4. If multiple versions, use the full path:
   /usr/bin/python3.12 -m venv myenv

5. Consider using pyenv for managing Python versions:
   pyenv install 3.12
   pyenv local 3.12
   python -m venv myenv

problem: pip dependency conflict: 'package requires different-package>=2.0, but you have different-package 1.5'
error_code: ERROR: pip's dependency resolver does not currently take into account all the packages that are installed
symptoms: Installing or upgrading a package causes dependency conflicts. pip warns that installed packages have incompatible version requirements.
attempted_steps: Tried pip install package, got dependency conflict warnings
supporting_evidence: Dependency conflicts occur when two or more packages require different versions of the same dependency.
verified_solution:
1. Start fresh with a new virtual environment:
   python -m venv clean_env
   clean_env\Scripts\activate
   pip install package_name

2. Use pip's resolver to see the conflict:
   pip check

3. Install conflicting packages in order:
   pip install package_a
   pip install package_b
   (pip will try to resolve automatically)

4. Pin specific compatible versions:
   pip install 'package_a==1.0' 'package_b>=2.0,<3.0'

5. Use pipdeptree to visualize dependencies:
   pip install pipdeptree
   pipdeptree --warn

problem: git clone fails with 'fatal: repository not found' even though the URL is correct
error_code: fatal: repository 'https://github.com/user/repo.git/' not found
symptoms: git clone fails with repository not found error. The URL is correct and the repository exists on GitHub but is private.
attempted_steps: Tried git clone https://github.com/user/private-repo.git
supporting_evidence: GitHub returns 'not found' instead of 'access denied' for private repositories to avoid revealing that the repository exists.
verified_solution:
1. Check if you're authenticated:
   git config --global user.name
   git config --global user.email

2. For HTTPS, use a Personal Access Token:
   - Go to GitHub Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens
   - Generate a token with 'repo' scope
   - Clone with: git clone https://TOKEN@github.com/user/repo.git

3. For SSH:
   ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C 'your@email.com'
   # Add public key to GitHub
   git clone git@github.com:user/repo.git

4. Use GitHub CLI:
   gh auth login
   gh repo clone user/repo

problem: Python UnicodeDecodeError when reading files with non-ASCII characters
error_code: UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte
symptoms: Opening a file with open() fails with UnicodeDecodeError. The file contains special characters, emojis, or non-English text.
attempted_steps: Tried open('file.txt', 'r') to read the file
supporting_evidence: On Windows, Python's default encoding is often 'cp1252' (Windows-1252), not UTF-8. Files with UTF-8 encoded characters fail to decode.
verified_solution:
1. Specify UTF-8 encoding explicitly:
   with open('file.txt', 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
       content = f.read()

2. If encoding is unknown, use errors parameter:
   with open('file.txt', 'r', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') as f:
       content = f.read()

3. Detect encoding with chardet:
   pip install chardet
   import chardet
   with open('file.txt', 'rb') as f:
       result = chardet.detect(f.read())
   encoding = result['encoding']

4. Set UTF-8 as default (Python 3.7+):
   Set environment variable: PYTHONUTF8=1
   Or run: python -X utf8 script.py

problem: git stash pop fails with merge conflicts
error_code: CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in file.py; stash pop failed
symptoms: After stashing changes with git stash, switching branches, and then popping the stash, conflicts occur. The stash remains in the stash list even after the failed pop.
attempted_steps: git stash, git checkout other-branch, did some work, git checkout main, git stash pop
supporting_evidence: git stash pop applies stashed changes and can conflict with changes made since the stash was created.
verified_solution:
1. Resolve the conflicts in the affected files
2. Stage resolved files:
   git add resolved_file.py
3. The stash is NOT automatically dropped after a failed pop
4. Once resolved, manually drop the stash:
   git stash drop

To avoid conflicts in the future:
- Use git stash apply instead of pop (doesn't auto-drop)
- Create a branch from stash: git stash branch new-branch
- Commit your changes before switching branches instead of stashing

problem: pip install editable mode fails: 'does not appear to be a Python project'
error_code: ERROR: file:///path/to/project does not appear to be a Python project: neither 'setup.py' nor 'pyproject.toml' found
symptoms: Running pip install -e . fails because the project directory doesn't have setup.py or pyproject.toml.
attempted_steps: Navigated to project directory and ran pip install -e .
supporting_evidence: Editable installs require a project configuration file that defines the package metadata.
verified_solution:
1. Create a minimal pyproject.toml:
   [build-system]
   requires = ['setuptools>=64']
   build-backend = 'setuptools.backends._legacy:_Backend'

   [project]
   name = 'your-package'
   version = '0.1.0'

2. Or create a minimal setup.py:
   from setuptools import setup, find_packages
   setup(name='your-package', packages=find_packages())

3. Make sure you're in the right directory:
   ls  # should show your Python package directory
   pip install -e .

4. For modern projects, pyproject.toml is preferred over setup.py

problem: pip install fails with 'error: externally-managed-environment' on modern Linux (Ubuntu 23+, Debian 12+)
error_code: error: externally-managed-environment (PEP 668)
symptoms: Running pip install package fails with a warning that the system Python environment is externally managed by apt and installing packages may break OS packages.
attempted_steps: Ran pip install package, tried sudo pip install package
supporting_evidence: PEP 668 prevents installing packages globally using pip on modern Linux distributions to prevent corrupting system apt packages.
verified_solution:
1. Recommended: Create a virtual environment:
   python3 -m venv ~/myenv
   source ~/myenv/bin/activate
   pip install package_name

2. Alternative for standalone CLI tools: Use pipx
   sudo apt install pipx
   pipx install package_name

3. Override (not recommended for system stability):
   pip install --break-system-packages package_name

problem: pip install fails with 'SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed'
error_code: SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED]
symptoms: pip cannot download any package from PyPI. Network connection terminates with SSL certificate verification error, common behind corporate firewalls or VPNs.
attempted_steps: Retried pip install, checked internet connection in browser
supporting_evidence: Python's pip uses its own certifi certificate bundle. Corporate firewalls or missing root CA certs cause certificate verification to fail.
verified_solution:
1. Upgrade certifi bundle:
   python -m pip install --upgrade certifi

2. Configure trusted hosts in pip.ini / pip.conf:
   pip install --trusted-host pypi.org --trusted-host files.pythonhosted.org package_name

3. On corporate networks with custom certs:
   pip config set global.cert /path/to/corporate-ca-bundle.crt

problem: pip install fails with 'PermissionError: [WinError 5] Access is denied' while upgrading pip itself
error_code: PermissionError: [WinError 5] Access is denied: 'pip.exe'
symptoms: Running 'pip install --upgrade pip' removes parts of the old pip executable while it is still running, leaving pip in a broken, half-installed state.
attempted_steps: Ran pip install --upgrade pip directly in command prompt
supporting_evidence: On Windows, an active running binary (pip.exe) cannot be overwritten in-place by itself.
verified_solution:
1. Run the upgrade using Python's module flag instead of pip executable directly:
   python -m pip install --upgrade pip

2. If pip is already broken, reinstall using ensurepip:
   python -m ensurepip --upgrade

problem: pip install fails with 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named distutils' on Python 3.12
error_code: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'distutils'
symptoms: Building older packages or running legacy setup.py scripts on Python 3.12 fails with missing distutils module.
attempted_steps: Tried pip install distutils
supporting_evidence: distutils was deprecated in Python 3.10 and completely removed from the standard library in Python 3.12 (PEP 632). Setuptools now provides a standalone replacement.
verified_solution:
1. Install and upgrade setuptools which provides a vendored distutils:
   python -m pip install --upgrade setuptools

2. Set environment variable to use setuptools distutils:
   export SETUPTOOLS_USE_DISTUTILS=stdlib (Linux/macOS)
   set SETUPTOOLS_USE_DISTUTILS=stdlib (Windows)

3. If possible, upgrade the target package to a newer version that uses pyproject.toml / setuptools instead of raw distutils.

problem: ImportError: cannot import name 'X' from partially initialized module 'Y' (circular import)
error_code: ImportError: cannot import name ... (most likely due to a circular import)
symptoms: Running a Python script fails during module loading with an ImportError stating that an object cannot be imported from a partially initialized module.
attempted_steps: Checked spelling of imported function, verified function exists in target file
supporting_evidence: Occurs when Module A imports Module B while Module B simultaneously imports Module A before Module A has finished executing its top-level definitions.
verified_solution:
1. Restructure code: Move shared functions, classes, or types into a third common module (e.g. models.py or utils.py) that both modules import.

2. Move the import inside the function/method where it is actually used (deferred local import) rather than at top of file.

3. For typing hints only, use TYPE_CHECKING guard:
   from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
   if TYPE_CHECKING:
       from module_b import ClassB

problem: RuntimeError: This event loop is already running when executing asyncio in Jupyter / IPython
error_code: RuntimeError: This event loop is already running
symptoms: Calling asyncio.run(main()) inside Jupyter Notebook, IPython shell, or an existing async framework raises RuntimeError.
attempted_steps: Tried asyncio.run(), tried loop = asyncio.get_event_loop(); loop.run_until_complete()
supporting_evidence: Jupyter Notebook runs inside an active Tornado/asyncio event loop. Python's standard asyncio.run() creates a new loop and fails if an event loop is already active on the current thread.
verified_solution:
1. In Jupyter Notebook / IPython, directly await the coroutine without asyncio.run:
   await main()

2. Or use nest_asyncio to allow nested event loops:
   import nest_asyncio
   nest_asyncio.apply()
   asyncio.run(main())

problem: AttributeError: module 'collections' has no attribute 'MutableMapping' on Python 3.10+
error_code: AttributeError: module 'collections' has no attribute 'MutableMapping'
symptoms: Importing older third-party libraries fails with AttributeError when referencing collections.MutableMapping or collections.Mapping.
attempted_steps: Reinstalled package, checked python version
supporting_evidence: In Python 3.10, abstract collection classes were completely removed from the root 'collections' module and moved into 'collections.abc'.
verified_solution:
1. Upgrade the problematic library to its latest release where this deprecation is fixed:
   pip install --upgrade package_name

2. If the package is unmaintained, patch imports in your script before importing the package:
   import collections.abc
   import collections
   collections.MutableMapping = collections.abc.MutableMapping
   collections.Mapping = collections.abc.Mapping

problem: ImportError: libGL.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory when importing cv2 (OpenCV)
error_code: ImportError: libGL.so.1: cannot open shared object file
symptoms: import cv2 fails in Docker containers or minimal Linux servers with missing shared C library libGL.so.1.
attempted_steps: pip install opencv-python, retried inside container
supporting_evidence: opencv-python requires OpenGL and system GUI libraries that are absent in minimal Docker images and headless Linux servers.
verified_solution:
1. Recommended: Use the headless build of OpenCV which does not require GUI/OpenGL shared libraries:
   pip uninstall opencv-python
   pip install opencv-python-headless

2. Or install the missing OS libraries on Debian/Ubuntu:
   sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y libgl1-mesa-glx libglib2.0-0

problem: Git error: 'fatal: refusing to merge unrelated histories' during git pull
error_code: fatal: refusing to merge unrelated histories
symptoms: Pulling from a newly initialized remote GitHub repository into a local repository that was independently initialized fails.
attempted_steps: git pull origin main
supporting_evidence: Git refuses to merge branches that do not share a common commit history to protect against accidental branch collisions.
verified_solution:
1. Force Git to allow merging unrelated histories:
   git pull origin main --allow-unrelated-histories

2. Resolve any file conflicts that occur (e.g. README.md or .gitignore)
3. Commit the merge:
   git commit -m 'Merge remote repository and allow unrelated histories'
4. Push back to remote:
   git push origin main

problem: Git error: 'error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge'
error_code: error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge
symptoms: Running git pull or git checkout fails because uncommitted modifications exist in files that are also modified on the incoming branch.
attempted_steps: git pull origin main
supporting_evidence: Git prevents destructive overwriting of uncommitted working directory changes.
verified_solution:
Option 1: Save local work temporarily with stash, pull, then re-apply:
   git stash
   git pull origin main
   git stash pop

Option 2: If local changes are complete, commit them first:
   git add .
   git commit -m 'Save local work before pull'
   git pull origin main

Option 3: Discard local changes completely if unneeded:
   git checkout -- filename.py  (or git reset --hard HEAD)

problem: Git error: 'fatal: remote origin already exists' when running git remote add
error_code: fatal: remote origin already exists
symptoms: Attempting to link a repository to a remote via 'git remote add origin URL' fails because the remote name 'origin' is already defined.
attempted_steps: git remote add origin https://github.com/user/repo.git
supporting_evidence: Each remote name in a Git repository must be unique.
verified_solution:
1. Update the existing remote URL instead of adding a new one:
   git remote set-url origin https://github.com/user/repo.git

2. Or delete the old remote first:
   git remote remove origin
   git remote add origin https://github.com/user/repo.git

3. Verify configured remotes:
   git remote -v

problem: Git error: 'Permission denied (publickey)' when cloning or pushing via SSH
error_code: Permission denied (publickey)
symptoms: Connecting to GitHub/GitLab over git@github.com:... fails with public key permission denied.
attempted_steps: git clone git@github.com:user/repo.git
supporting_evidence: SSH agent does not have your private key loaded, or the corresponding public key was not added to your GitHub/GitLab account settings.
verified_solution:
1. Check if SSH key exists:
   ls -la ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub or ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub

2. Generate key if missing:
   ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C 'your_email@example.com'

3. Start ssh-agent and add key:
   eval $(ssh-agent -s)
   ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519

4. Copy public key and paste into GitHub (Settings > SSH and GPG keys):
   cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub

5. Test connection:
   ssh -T git@github.com

problem: Git error: 'RPC failed; HTTP 413 curl 22 The requested URL returned error: 413 Payload Too Large'
error_code: RPC failed; HTTP 413 curl 22
symptoms: Pushing a repository containing large files or deep commit history fails when using HTTPS due to HTTP buffer size limits.
attempted_steps: git push origin main
supporting_evidence: The default HTTP postBuffer in git config is typically 1MB, which is exceeded during large pushes over HTTPS.
verified_solution:
1. Increase Git HTTP postBuffer to 500MB:
   git config --global http.postBuffer 524288000

2. Or switch remote from HTTPS to SSH which does not have HTTP request size limitations:
   git remote set-url origin git@github.com:username/repository.git

3. If pushing files over 100MB, use Git LFS (Large File Storage):
   git lfs install
   git lfs track '*.psd' '*.zip' '*.bin'

problem: Git repository submodules are empty folders after cloning
error_code: Submodule folder is empty after git clone
symptoms: After cloning a repository that uses submodules, the submodule directories are completely empty.
attempted_steps: git clone repo_url
supporting_evidence: By default, git clone does not fetch submodule repository content unless explicitly instructed.
verified_solution:
1. If already cloned, initialize and update submodules:
   git submodule update --init --recursive

2. For future clones, clone submodules automatically in one command:
   git clone --recurse-submodules repo_url

problem: Docker container run fails: 'Bind for 0.0.0.0:8000 failed: port is already allocated'
error_code: Bind for 0.0.0.0:8000 failed: port is already allocated
symptoms: Running docker run -p 8000:8000 fails because another process or another container is currently listening on port 8000.
attempted_steps: docker run -p 8000:8000 image_name
supporting_evidence: Only one process can bind to a host network interface port at a time.
verified_solution:
1. Find and kill the conflicting process on Windows:
   netstat -ano | findstr :8000
   taskkill /PID <PID_NUMBER> /F

   On Linux/macOS:
   lsof -i :8000
   kill -9 <PID_NUMBER>

2. Check for running Docker containers occupying the port:
   docker ps
   docker stop <container_id>

3. Or map to an alternate host port:
   docker run -p 8080:8000 image_name

problem: Docker container exits immediately with code 137 (OOMKilled - Out of Memory)
error_code: Exited (137) / OOMKilled
symptoms: A container running machine learning, compilation, or high-memory tasks abruptly stops with exit code 137.
attempted_steps: docker restart container_name
supporting_evidence: Exit code 137 indicates the process received SIGKILL (signal 9 + 128 = 137), typically dispatched by the Linux kernel Out-Of-Memory (OOM) killer when RAM limits are exceeded.
verified_solution:
1. Verify OOMKilled status:
   docker inspect container_name --format '{{.State.OOMKilled}}'

2. Increase container memory limit in docker run:
   docker run -m 4g --memory-swap 6g image_name

3. In Docker Desktop (Windows/macOS), increase allocated VM memory:
   Settings > Resources > Advanced > Increase Memory slider to 8GB+

problem: Linux error: 'Could not get lock /var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend' when running apt install
error_code: Could not get lock /var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend - open (11: Resource temporarily unavailable)
symptoms: Running sudo apt-get update or install fails with lock-frontend error. Another package manager process is holding the lock.
attempted_steps: sudo apt install package
supporting_evidence: Debian/Ubuntu dpkg package manager locks its database during background automatic updates (unattended-upgrades).
verified_solution:
1. Wait 1-2 minutes for unattended-upgrades to finish, or check what process holds the lock:
   ps aux | grep -i apt

2. If a process is stuck, terminate it:
   sudo killall apt apt-get unattended-upgr

3. If lock files remain stale after crash, remove them and configure dpkg:
   sudo rm /var/lib/apt/lists/lock
   sudo rm /var/cache/apt/archives/lock
   sudo rm /var/lib/dpkg/lock*
   sudo dpkg --configure -a

problem: Jupyter Notebook does not recognize packages installed in virtual environment
error_code: ModuleNotFoundError in Jupyter notebook despite pip install inside venv
symptoms: Package is verified installed via 'pip list' in terminal venv, but running the notebook kernel still throws ModuleNotFoundError.
attempted_steps: Activated venv, ran pip install package, launched jupyter notebook
supporting_evidence: Jupyter notebooks execute against registered kernels (ipykernel). If the venv kernel was not registered, Jupyter defaults to the global Python interpreter.
verified_solution:
1. Activate your virtual environment:
   myenv\Scripts\activate (Windows) or source myenv/bin/activate (Linux)

2. Install ipykernel in the virtual environment:
   pip install ipykernel

3. Register the virtual environment as a selectable Jupyter kernel:
   python -m ipykernel install --user --name=myenv --display-name 'Python (myenv)'

4. Launch Jupyter, open your notebook, and change kernel: Kernel > Change Kernel > Python (myenv)

problem: Poetry error: 'The currently activated Python version is not supported by the project'
error_code: The currently activated Python version is not supported by the project (^3.10)
symptoms: Running poetry install fails because your active system Python does not match pyproject.toml python requirement.
attempted_steps: poetry install
supporting_evidence: Poetry enforces strict Python version compatibility specified under [tool.poetry.dependencies] python in pyproject.toml.
verified_solution:
1. Tell Poetry to use an exact installed Python executable:
   poetry env use /usr/bin/python3.10  (or path to python3.11/py.exe)

2. If using pyenv, select the version first:
   pyenv local 3.10.12
   poetry env use $(which python)

3. Or update pyproject.toml if your code supports newer Python versions:
   [tool.poetry.dependencies]
   python = '>=3.10,<3.13'
   and run: poetry lock --no-update

problem: Git error: 'File exceeds GitHub's file size limit of 100.00 MB' on push
error_code: GH001: Large files detected. File X is 150.00 MB; this exceeds GitHub's file size limit
symptoms: git push fails with remote rejection because a commit contains a binary dataset or model checkpoint exceeding 100MB.
attempted_steps: Deleted file and made a new commit, git push still fails
supporting_evidence: Simply deleting the file in a subsequent commit leaves the large blob in Git commit history. The commit containing the blob must be rewritten or tracked via Git LFS.
verified_solution:
1. Undo the last commit while keeping files in working directory:
   git reset --soft HEAD~1

2. Track the large file using Git LFS:
   git lfs install
   git lfs track '*.zip'
   git add .gitattributes

3. If the file is already committed several commits back, remove it using git filter-repo:
   pip install git-filter-repo
   git filter-repo --path path/to/large_file.zip --invert-paths

4. Push with LFS:
   git push origin main --force

problem: Conda environment creation fails: 'ResolvePackageNotFound: - python=3.12'
error_code: ResolvePackageNotFound
symptoms: Running conda create -n myenv python=3.12 fails because default channels do not have the requested build or package version for the current platform architecture.
attempted_steps: conda create -n myenv python=3.12
supporting_evidence: The default anaconda channel often lags behind conda-forge for recent package releases and specific platform builds (e.g. ARM64 / Apple Silicon).
verified_solution:
1. Use the community-maintained conda-forge channel:
   conda create -n myenv -c conda-forge python=3.12

2. Configure conda-forge as the highest priority default channel:
   conda config --add channels conda-forge
   conda config --set channel_priority strict
   conda create -n myenv python=3.12

problem: pip install fails with 'error: command gcc failed: No such file or directory' on Linux
error_code: error: command 'gcc' failed: No such file or directory
symptoms: Installing packages that contain C/C++ extensions fails during the setup.py bdist_wheel phase with missing gcc compiler error.
attempted_steps: pip install uwsgi (or cffi, cryptography, psycopg2)
supporting_evidence: Packages distributing C source code without pre-compiled manylinux wheels require gcc and Python C headers installed on the host OS.
verified_solution:
1. Install build-essential and Python development headers on Debian/Ubuntu:
   sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y build-essential python3-dev

2. On CentOS / RHEL / Fedora:
   sudo dnf groupinstall -y 'Development Tools' && sudo dnf install -y python3-devel

3. Retry pip install:
   pip install package_name

problem: TypeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable when returning API response
error_code: TypeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable
symptoms: Calling json.dumps(data) on a dictionary containing datetime objects or returning raw dictionaries from web endpoints fails with TypeError.
attempted_steps: json.dumps(data)
supporting_evidence: Python's built-in json module only supports basic primitives (str, int, float, bool, list, dict, None) by default and does not serialize datetime instances.

problem: Git error: 'fatal: cannot do a partial commit during a merge'
error_code: fatal: cannot do a partial commit during a merge
symptoms: Running 'git commit filename.py -m "fix"' while in the middle of a merge or conflict resolution raises fatal partial commit error.
attempted_steps: git commit filename.py -m 'message'
supporting_evidence: Git requires all resolved conflicts to be staged together to complete a merge commit; committing individual files separately during an active merge is prohibited.
verified_solution:
1. Stage the resolved files using git add:
   git add filename.py

2. Commit without specifying individual file paths:
   git commit -m 'Resolve merge conflict in filename.py'

3. Or abort the merge if started by mistake:
   git merge --abort

problem: Git error: 'fatal: not a valid object name: HEAD' in fresh empty repository
error_code: fatal: not a valid object name: 'HEAD'
symptoms: Running git log, git branch, or git status on a newly initialized git repository (git init) outputs object name error.
attempted_steps: git init, git branch, git log
supporting_evidence: A brand new Git repository has no commits yet. The HEAD pointer references a branch that will only be materialized after the initial commit.
verified_solution:
1. Create and commit your first file to initialize the HEAD pointer:
   git add .
   git commit -m 'Initial commit'

2. Now git log and git branch will work normally:
   git log
   git branch -M main

problem: Git interactive rebase conflict: 'Interactive rebase stopped at commit' / how to continue
error_code: Interactive rebase stopped at commit / Could not apply
symptoms: During git rebase -i or git pull --rebase, Git pauses execution due to conflicting changes on a replayed commit.
attempted_steps: git rebase -i HEAD~3
supporting_evidence: Git stops at the exact commit where conflicts occur so the developer can resolve them before continuing the replay sequence.
verified_solution:
1. Check conflicted files:
   git status

2. Open files and resolve conflict markers (<<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>>)
3. Stage resolved files (DO NOT run git commit):
   git add resolved_file.py

4. Continue rebase:
   git rebase --continue

5. If rebase gets completely mangled and you want to cancel:
   git rebase --abort

problem: Git: Remove tracked file from repository without deleting it from local disk
error_code: Untrack file without deleting local copy
symptoms: A config file (.env or config.json) was accidentally committed and pushed to remote, but deleting it locally breaks local application runs.
attempted_steps: git rm filename (deletes the local file too)
supporting_evidence: Standard 'git rm' deletes both the repository index reference and the working tree file. Using '--cached' removes it only from version control.
verified_solution:
1. Remove from Git index only (keeps local file untouched):
   git rm --cached .env

2. Add the file to .gitignore so it won't be re-tracked:
   echo '.env' >> .gitignore

3. Commit and push the removal:
   git add .gitignore
   git commit -m 'Stop tracking .env file'
   git push origin main

problem: Docker build fails: 'COPY failed: file not found in build context'
error_code: COPY failed: file not found in build context
symptoms: Running docker build -t myapp . fails on a COPY instruction stating that the source file or directory does not exist.
attempted_steps: docker build -t myapp .
supporting_evidence: Docker can only COPY files that exist inside the specified build context (the directory passed at the end of the docker build command). It cannot reach parent directories via '../'.
verified_solution:
1. Verify you are running docker build from the root directory that contains all required files:
   docker build -t myapp .

2. Check your .dockerignore file to ensure the target file is not accidentally excluded.

3. Ensure file path casing matches exactly (Linux container builds are strictly case-sensitive).

4. If referencing files outside directory, specify build context explicitly:
   docker build -f docker/Dockerfile -t myapp .

problem: pip install fails with 'ReadTimeoutError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host=pypi.org): Read timed out'
error_code: pip._vendor.urllib3.exceptions.ReadTimeoutError
symptoms: Downloading large packages (PyTorch, TensorFlow, CUDA wheels) fails mid-download on slow or unstable network connections.
attempted_steps: Retried pip install multiple times
supporting_evidence: pip has a default socket read timeout of 15 seconds, which easily triggers when downloading multi-gigabyte wheels over high-latency networks.
verified_solution:
1. Increase pip default timeout to 120 seconds or higher:
   pip install --default-timeout=120 package_name

2. Configure timeout permanently in pip.ini / pip.conf:
   pip config set global.timeout 120

3. For PyTorch specifically, use the official dedicated mirror:
   pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121

problem: UnboundLocalError: local variable 'x' referenced before assignment in Python function
error_code: UnboundLocalError: local variable referenced before assignment
symptoms: A function that reads an outer/global variable raises UnboundLocalError when that variable is also assigned to anywhere inside the function body.
attempted_steps: Checked value of variable before calling function
supporting_evidence: When Python sees an assignment (e.g. x = ...) anywhere inside a function, it classifies that variable as local for the entire scope. Referencing it before the assignment triggers UnboundLocalError.
verified_solution:
Option 1: Declare the variable as global inside the function:
   x = 10
   def update():
       global x
       x += 1

Option 2: For nested functions, declare as nonlocal:
   def outer():
       x = 10
       def inner():
           nonlocal x
           x += 1

Option 3: Pass variable explicitly as argument and return updated value (cleanest functional pattern):
   def update(x):
       return x + 1

problem: pip install fails with 'ERROR: Wheel tag not supported on this platform'
error_code: ERROR: ... is not a supported wheel on this platform
symptoms: Attempting to install a manually downloaded .whl file fails with unsupported wheel tag error.
attempted_steps: pip install package-1.0.0-cp310-cp310-win_amd64.whl on Python 3.12
supporting_evidence: Wheel filenames encode the Python version (cp310 = Python 3.10), ABI, and OS architecture (win_amd64 vs linux_x86_64). Attempting to install across mismatched versions or 32-bit/64-bit architectures is rejected.
verified_solution:
1. Check your exact supported wheel tags in current Python:
   pip debug --verbose

2. Download the wheel file matching your exact Python version (e.g. cp312 for Python 3.12) and architecture (win_amd64 for 64-bit Windows).

3. Or install directly from PyPI so pip automatically selects the compatible wheel:
   pip install package_name

problem: Git: Accidentally committed changes to 'main' instead of a feature branch
error_code: Commits made to wrong local branch
symptoms: Developer made 3 commits directly on local 'main' branch before creating a feature branch, and hasn't pushed yet.
attempted_steps: git branch feature-branch
supporting_evidence: Branches in Git are lightweight movable pointers. You can move commits to a new branch and reset the main pointer back without losing any work.
verified_solution:
1. Create the new feature branch at current commit (retains all commits):
   git branch feature-branch

2. Reset main back to the remote origin/main state (removes commits from main):
   git reset --keep origin/main  (or git reset --hard HEAD~3)

3. Switch to your new feature branch where all your commits exist:
   git switch feature-branch

4. Your work is now safely on feature-branch and main is clean!

problem: Docker volume mount fails with 'EACCES: permission denied' inside Linux container
error_code: EACCES: permission denied, open /app/data
symptoms: A container running as a non-root user (e.g. node, appuser) cannot write to host-mounted volume directories (-v $(pwd)/data:/app/data).
attempted_steps: docker run -v ./data:/app/data image_name
supporting_evidence: Linux containers share user and group IDs (UID/GID) with the host filesystem. If the container user UID does not have write permissions on host folder, operations fail with EACCES.
verified_solution:
Option 1: Pass matching host user UID and GID to docker run:
   docker run --user $(id -u):$(id -g) -v $(pwd)/data:/app/data image_name

Option 2: Adjust ownership of host directory before mounting:
   sudo chown -R 1000:1000 ./data

Option 3: In Dockerfile, ensure working directory permissions are granted to the user:
   RUN chown -R appuser:appgroup /app/data

problem: RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded in comparison in Python
error_code: RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded
symptoms: Python script crashes when traversing recursive data structures, deeply nested trees/graphs, or when recursive functions lack base termination condition.
attempted_steps: Checked call stack in traceback
supporting_evidence: Python's default recursion limit is 1000 frames to protect against C-level stack overflow crashes.
verified_solution:
1. Verify recursive base condition exists and terminates correctly.

2. Convert recursive algorithm to iterative using an explicit stack/queue (recommended for large trees).

3. If deep recursion is required for valid algorithmic traversal (e.g. deep AST parsing):
   import sys
   sys.setrecursionlimit(5000)

problem: Git error: 'warning: CRLF will be replaced by LF' / line ending normalization
error_code: warning: CRLF will be replaced by LF in file.txt. The file will have its original line endings in your working directory
symptoms: Staging files on Windows warns that CRLF carriage returns will be replaced by LF line feeds, causing spurious diffs across cross-platform teams.
attempted_steps: git add .
supporting_evidence: Windows uses Carriage Return + Line Feed (CRLF, \r\n) while Linux/macOS uses Line Feed (LF, \n). Git autocrlf settings normalize endings.
verified_solution:
1. For Windows developers, configure Git to convert CRLF to LF on commit:
   git config --global core.autocrlf true

2. Best practice for projects: Create a .gitattributes file in repo root:
   * text=auto
   *.py text eol=lf
   *.sh text eol=lf
   *.bat text eol=crlf

3. Renormalize repository line endings:
   git add --renormalize .
